title: Perimeter Worksheets: Rectangles
intro: Teach perimeter as one complete trip around a boundary.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Trace each side of a rectangle and label its length. Add all four lengths, noting that opposite sides match.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

6 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 18 units

You can also add the two different lengths and double: 2 × (6 + 3) = 18.

Ask your student

Have we counted every side exactly once?

If your student needs help

If the student multiplies side lengths, contrast the outline with the surface inside it.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each set has six distinct pairs of side lengths from 2 through 9 units. The original diagrams and numerical answers are preserved. The answer key gives the total perimeter. Use the space below each picture to record a sum that shows all four sides.
